response.sql: SELECT t.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS avg_bandusage_pct, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE t.observstation NOT IN (SELECT observstation FROM telescopes WHERE equipstatus = 'Maintenance') GROUP BY t.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC, station, moon_phase LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Telescopes with a NULL lunarstage in their observatory form their own moon-phase group, so they appear in the results as a NULL moon phase. The request only says to ignore missing values for bandusagepct.
The maintenance exclusion uses every telescope at a station. Telescopes without a matching observatory cannot affect the result because the inner join drops them anyway.
Each telescope matches at most one observatory, since observatories.observstation is the primary key, so COUNT of telescregistry counts telescopes and not duplicate join rows.
Ties in telescope_count are broken by station and then moon phase, which the request does not specify.

alternatives.interpretation: Drop moon-phase groups whose lunarstage is missing, so only stations with a recorded moon phase are reported.
alternatives.sql: SELECT t.observstation AS station, o.lunarstage AS moon_phase, AVG(t.bandusagepct) AS avg_bandusage_pct, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM telescopes t JOIN observatories o ON o.observstation = t.observstation WHERE o.lunarstage IS NOT NULL AND t.observstation NOT IN (SELECT observstation FROM telescopes WHERE equipstatus = 'Maintenance') GROUP BY t.observstation, o.lunarstage ORDER BY telescope_count DESC, station, moon_phase LIMIT 10;
